title: AI adoption more than doubles in almost every EU strategic sector
content: According to a new EU analysis, the share of firms using AI in the EU’s 10 strategic sectors grew from 7% in 2021 to 18% in 2025. Media, energy and electronic sectors lead in AI adoption, while mobility, tourism and agri-food lag behind. This uneven growth is driven mainly by general-purpose AI.

title: Turning 18? Apply for a free DiscoverEU travel pass
content: The EU is offering DiscoverEU travel passes to 18-year-olds to explore Europe by train. Applications are open until 15 October 2026 at midday Brussels time. You can travel anytime between 1 March 2027 and 31 May 2028 for up to 7 days within a one-month period.

title: Making data centres energy efficient thanks to a new EU rating system
content: The rapid growth in data centres puts pressure on electricity grids and the use of natural resources, as well as contributes to increased carbon emissions. To limit these impacts, the European Commission has proposed a common rating scheme for data centres aimed at increasing energy transparency.

title: EU KIDS Act: helping children navigate a safer online world
content: In the face of growing concerns about the risks children and teenagers face when using online platforms, the EU has proposed a new KIDS Act. This will introduce a gradual uptake of social media for children in the EU, notably delaying access to social media until the age of 13.

title: Guaranteeing social rights for workers everywhere in the EU
content: The Commission has adopted proposals that will guarantee social rights for workers, regardless of where they choose to live in the EU. Workers will be able to have their professional skills understood everywhere in the EU and prove and claim their social security and health insurance rights.

title: Realising the potential of the EU’s outermost regions
content: A new Commission strategy will ensure that the EU’s outermost regions can fully realise their potential, with stronger support, greater resilience and fairer opportunities for their people. From Martinique to Madeira, the EU’s outermost regions play a key geostrategic role in today’s changing world.
